summary: Describes use cases for Network Virtualization over Layer 3 (NVO3), which are overlay networks in data centers. It looks at how such overlays can serve different data-center applications. It is informational background.

eli5.summary: Imagine many pretend roads drawn on top of one real road system, so different groups think they have their own private streets.

what is network virtualization over layer 3
subtitle: Overlays for virtual networks in modern data centers

tldr.problem: Traditional data center networks using VLANs cannot scale to support the number of isolated virtual networks needed for modern cloud applications and multi-tenant services.
tldr.mechanism: Network Virtualization over Layer 3 (NVO3) uses overlay tunnels to decouple virtual networks from physical infrastructure, allowing many independent virtual networks to run on the same physical network.
tldr.outcome: Data centers can support thousands of isolated virtual networks, scale VM workloads elastically, and allow tenants to manage their own address spaces.

today: RFC 8151 is an Informational RFC from May 2017 describing use cases and deployment scenarios for NVO3 technology. Data center providers and cloud services use NVO3 extensively to support multi-tenant environments and scale virtual infrastructure.

sections.title: Virtual Networks Over Physical Infrastructure
sections.content:
Network Virtualization over Layer 3 (NVO3) is a technique for creating independent virtual networks on top of a shared physical data center network. Instead of being limited by the number of VLANs a switch can handle, an NVO3 system can support thousands of virtual networks running simultaneously on the same hardware.

The core idea is straightforward: traffic from a virtual network is encapsulated in a tunnel at one edge device, carried across the physical network, and unwrapped at the destination. This decoupling lets data center operators manage virtual networks independently from the physical wiring, and it lets tenants use their own address spaces without worrying about conflicts.
sections.eli5: Instead of drawing roads on top of the actual road system, think of NVO3 like wrapping packages in envelopes, mailing them through the actual roads, and unwrapping them at the destination.

sections.title: How NVO3 Works
sections.content:
NVO3 introduces an edge device at each point where virtual networks start and stop, called a Network Virtualization Edge (NVE). When a virtual machine wants to send traffic, the NVE encapsulates it with a tunnel header and a network identifier (VNID), then sends it through the physical network. When traffic arrives at another NVE, that device strips off the tunnel header using the VNID and delivers the packet to the right virtual network.

The NVE can run on a physical server, a VM, or a network appliance. Because the tunnels are just IP packets in the physical network, NVO3 works on top of any Layer 3 infrastructure without requiring special physical equipment.
sections.eli5: The NVE is like a mail sorter who wraps outgoing mail in labeled envelopes and removes envelopes from incoming mail to deliver it to the right mailbox.

sections.title: Real Data Center Deployments
sections.content:
Data centers deploy NVO3 in several practical scenarios. A data center provider might use NVO3 to offer isolated virtual networks to different customer tenants, each with their own virtual machines and address space. Customers can connect to these networks through the Internet using IPsec VPN tunnels or through a service provider's WAN VPN.

Within a single data center, NVO3 also solves the problem of mixed technology: some servers may use VXLAN encapsulation, others NVGRE, and some may not support overlay technology at all. A virtual gateway can translate between these different technologies, so all servers appear to be on the same logical network even though they use different protocols underneath.
sections.eli5: A data center can now serve customers who speak different languages by having a translator device that converts between them.

sections.title: Scaling Applications and Infrastructure
sections.content:
One key benefit of NVO3 is flexibility in placing virtual machines. When an application needs more computing power, administrators can start new VMs on any available server without reconfiguring the network—the NVE automatically handles the routing. If a server becomes too busy, VMs can move to another server without changing their network identity or breaking active connections.

NVO3 also supports complex multi-tier applications. A data center can create separate virtual networks for a web tier, an application tier, and a database tier, then place security functions (like firewalls) between them. This isolation happens in software, so the data center provider doesn't need separate physical networks for each tier.
sections.eli5: A delivery company can move delivery trucks between routes without customers needing to change their addresses or get mail interrupted.

sections.title: Security and Isolation
sections.content:
NVO3 provides strong traffic isolation between virtual networks. One tenant's traffic is encapsulated and separated from another tenant's traffic, preventing accidental data leakage. However, the underlying physical network operators can observe and potentially modify traffic, so tenants should only trust data center operators they have a relationship with.

Data center operators must also protect their physical network from attacks by tenant applications. Throttling bandwidth per virtual network prevents a tenant from generating traffic floods that would affect other customers. Firewalls and other security functions running as VMs within the NVO3 overlay can enforce additional policies between different parts of an application.
sections.eli5: Each tenant gets their own sealed envelope for their mail, but the post office workers can see who sent it and who it's addressed to.
